items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 26 at 2:49PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Water levels are expected to rise to 1 to 1.5 feet above the
normal high tide line around the Kotzebue Sound and Chukchi Sea
Coast around late Sunday, peaking overnight and diminishing
rapidly on Monday morning due to gusty northwesterly winds
between 25 & 35 mph behind the cold front that has moved through.
items.areas: Kivalina and Red Dog Dock; Baldwin Peninsula; Northern Seward Peninsula; Shishmaref

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 26 at 2:42PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
An Arctic cold front is has been moving southeast from the
Chukchi Sea today. Total snow accumulations of 2-6" is possible
in the Brooks Range with less than an inch expected for most of
the Eastern Arctic Coast. Periods of freezing drizzle are possible
as the snow diminishes this afternoon and evening.
items.areas: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast; Central Arctic Plains; Romanzof Mountains

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued July 26 at 2:34PM AKDT until July 27 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation. Total snow accumulations between 2 and
6 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze.

* WHERE...Central Brooks Range.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel may be impacted.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Widespread 2 inches of snow accumulation is
expected in total with up to 6 inches possible at higher
elevations. Snow diminishes this evening with periods of freezing
drizzle being possible overnight.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 25 at 2:56PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
A cold front is expected to move southeast from the Chukchi Sea
Saturday night through Sunday morning. Gusty northwesterly winds
are expected across the Kotzebue Sound and Chukchi Sea Coast
Sunday following the front. Gusts on Sunday are expected to be
between 25 and 35 mph. Water levels are expected to rise to 1 to
1.5 feet above the normal high tide line late Sunday, peaking
overnight and diminishing rapidly Monday morning.
items.areas: Kivalina and Red Dog Dock; Baldwin Peninsula; Northern Seward Peninsula; Shishmaref
